cases.description: harmonization, abbreviated figures: per-figure essential/omittable/[+8] notation

expected.help: Each measure shows a figured-bass symbol below the staff. The figures name intervals above the bass — count up from the bass note to find those pitches, then press Lock Chord. Parentheses mark tones you may drop in sparse texture or double in four.
hints: Count from the bass: 3 = two staff steps up, 5 = four steps, 6 = five steps, 7 = six steps. The plain numbers are the ones you must keep; the parenthesized ones you may drop or double.

cases.description: harmonization, unabbreviated figures: per-target raw stack, 8 parenthesized as optional doubling

expected.help: This exercise uses unabbreviated figures — every interval above the bass is written, including the octave (8). The figures appear below the staff. Read each number as a generic interval from the bass and play those pitches.
hints: Per chord: (8)-6-3. The (8) is the bass doubled at the octave — optional.
The 8 is the bass doubled at the octave — optional. The other numbers are the intervals above the bass you must sound.

cases.description: identification, abbreviated figures: distinct-figure plain expansion table

expected.help: Choose the abbreviated figure. Abbreviations drop redundant intervals — 6 stands for 6-3, 7 for 7-5-3, 6/4 for 6-4, 4/2 (or 2) for 6-4-2. The figure names intervals above the bass, not a chord name.

cases.description: identification, unabbreviated figures: distinct raw stacks listed

expected.help: Choose the unabbreviated figure — list every generic interval above the bass, including the octave (8). A triad with the third in the bass is 8/6/3, not 6.
